summary:
The Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2025 amends titles 11 and 28, United States Code, to increase compensation for chapter 7 trustees, adjust bankruptcy fees to fund the United States Trustee System, and extend the terms of certain temporary bankruptcy judgeships.

Section 3 amends 11 U.S.C. § 330(b)(1) to increase chapter 7 trustee compensation from $45 to $105 per case, and repeals 11 U.S.C. § 330(e). It establishes a new statutory allocation for the remainder of fees collected under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(1)(A) after trustee compensation: $63.51 to the Treasury special fund under 28 U.S.C. § 1931, $25.00 to the special fund under section 10101(b) of the Deficit Reduction Act of 2005, and $51.49 to the United States Trustee System Fund under 28 U.S.C. § 589a. It further amends 28 U.S.C. § 589a(b)(1)(A) to replace a percentage-based allocation ("40.46 percent") with a fixed dollar amount ("$51.49 of the fees collected in each case"), and amends 28 U.S.C. § 589a(f)(1) by striking subparagraphs (B) and (C) and redesignating subparagraph (D) as subparagraph (B).

Section 4 amends 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6)(B) to extend the applicable period for quarterly chapter 11 fees from 5 years to 10 years, and modifies the fee schedule by inserting "the greater of" before the minimum percentage threshold and increasing the maximum percentage from 0.8 to 0.9. It amends 28 U.S.C. § 589a(f) to extend the fee deposit period from 2026 to 2031. It adds a provision requiring that, for fiscal years 2026 through 2031, $5,400,000 of fees collected under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6) be deposited in the general fund of the Treasury, with the remainder deposited as specified in 28 U.S.C. § 589a(f).

Section 5 amends section 4 of the Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2020 (28 U.S.C. § 152 note) and section 1003(b)(2)(A) of the Bankruptcy Judgeship Act of 2017 (28 U.S.C. § 152 note) to extend the terms of specified temporary bankruptcy judgeships from 5 years to 10 years.

Section 6 establishes the effective dates. Generally, the amendments take effect on the first day of the calendar quarter occurring on or after the date of enactment. Section 3 applies to chapter 7 cases commenced on or after October 1 occurring after enactment, and to chapter 11, 12, or 13 cases converted to chapter 7. Section 4 applies to chapter 11 cases commenced or pending on the general effective date, and to quarterly fees for disbursements made in calendar quarters beginning on or after the date of enactment.
